dimensions.name: deployment_cap
dimensions.description: How freely AI systems may be put on the market and used.
dimensions.positive_means: deployment is permissive: few limits on releasing and using AI systems
dimensions.negative_means: deployment is restricted: bans, licences and approvals before release

dimensions.name: transparency
dimensions.description: What providers must reveal about their systems and data.
dimensions.negative_means: little or no duty to disclose; secrecy is allowed

dimensions.name: enforcement
dimensions.description: How breaches of the rules are punished.
dimensions.positive_means: strong penalties and powers to compel compliance

dimensions.name: audit_intensity
dimensions.description: How closely systems are checked and monitored.

items.sentence: AI practices that present an unacceptable risk are banned outright.
A two-year moratorium applies to the deployment of facial recognition in public spaces.
High-risk systems require pre-market approval before they may be placed on the market.
A regulatory sandbox lets developers release experimental systems without a licence.
Open-source models released for research are exempt from deployment restrictions.
The use of social scoring systems by public authorities is prohibited.
No general-purpose model may be deployed without a licence issued by the authority.
Firms may freely deploy low-risk applications without prior notification.
A safe harbour allows small developers to launch products without prior review.
The authority may impose a deployment cap on the number of users served by an unassessed model.
Providers must disclose the data sources used to train each model.
Synthetic audio and video must be watermarked in a machine-readable format.
Decisions affecting individuals must meet explainability standards set by the regulator.
Developers may withhold model details that constitute a trade secret.
Technical documentation describing model architecture must be published before release.
Systems that interact with people must notify users that they are dealing with an AI.
Risk assessments submitted to the authority remain confidential and are not released to the public.
Model cards summarising capabilities and limits are mandatory for all general-purpose models.
Providers are under no obligation to publish evaluation results.
All high-risk systems must be entered in a public register.
Violations are punishable by fines of up to 7% of worldwide turnover.
Executives who knowingly conceal safety failures face criminal liability.
Compliance with the code of practice is voluntary and carries no sanction.
A first breach results only in a warning letter.
The authority may seek an injunction to withdraw a non-compliant system from the market.
A three-year grace period applies before any penalty can be imposed.
The regulator may revoke a provider's licence after repeated breaches.
Member states shall lay down effective and dissuasive penalties.
Firms that report their own breaches receive amnesty from penalties.
Providers bear strict liability for harm caused by their systems.
Each high-risk system must pass a third-party audit every year.
Providers may rely on a self-assessment instead of external review.
Deployed models are subject to continuous monitoring by the supervisory authority.
Officials may carry out an unannounced inspection of any data centre.
Serious malfunctions must be covered by incident reporting within 72 hours.
Low-risk systems are subject to no routine audits.
Frontier models must undergo independent red-teaming before release.
Systems must keep an audit trail of automated decisions for inspection.
Small providers benefit from reduced reporting duties.
A conformity assessment by a notified body is required before market entry.
The government establishes a framework for artificial intelligence.
Artificial intelligence is developing quickly in many sectors.
Member states shall designate a national contact point.
The authority publishes an annual work programme.
Stakeholders were consulted while the bill was drafted.
For the purposes of this act the following definitions apply.
The entry into force of this regulation is the twentieth day after publication.

AI is a global technology developed in many countries.
A committee advises the minister on technical matters.

Technology evolves faster than legislation.

dimensions.name: access_restriction
dimensions.description: How far the policy limits patients' access to treatments and services.
dimensions.positive_means: severe restrictions: authorisations, referrals and gatekeeping before care
dimensions.negative_means: open access: patients reach care without gatekeeping

dimensions.name: cost_sharing
dimensions.description: How much of the cost of care patients pay themselves.
dimensions.positive_means: high patient burden: deductibles, copayments and charges
dimensions.negative_means: care is free or nearly free to the patient

dimensions.name: provider_regulation
dimensions.description: The regulatory burden on providers and insurers.
dimensions.positive_means: extensive licensing, reporting and compliance duties

dimensions.name: coverage_mandate
dimensions.description: How much care plans are required to cover.
dimensions.positive_means: comprehensive mandated benefits with few exclusions
dimensions.negative_means: bare-bones coverage with many exclusions permitted

dimensions.name: consent_requirement
dimensions.description: What kind of agreement is needed before personal data is used.
dimensions.positive_means: strict: explicit, informed, opt-in consent is required
dimensions.negative_means: loose: implied consent, opt-out or no consent is enough

dimensions.name: data_minimisation
dimensions.description: How far collection, reuse and retention of data are limited.
dimensions.positive_means: strict limits on what is collected, how long it is kept and what it is reused for
dimensions.negative_means: data may be collected in bulk, kept and reused freely

dimensions.name: individual_rights
dimensions.description: What individuals can demand regarding their own data.
dimensions.positive_means: strong rights to access, correct, delete and move their data
dimensions.negative_means: few rights; requests can be refused or charged for

dimensions.name: enforcement
dimensions.description: How breaches of the rules are punished.

dimensions.name: carbon_pricing
dimensions.description: Whether and how much emitters pay for their emissions.
dimensions.positive_means: a high, broad price on emissions
dimensions.negative_means: low or no carbon price; exemptions and free permits

dimensions.name: emission_standards
dimensions.description: Binding limits and technical requirements on polluters and products.

dimensions.name: green_subsidies
dimensions.description: Public financial support for clean technology.
dimensions.positive_means: generous public funding for clean technology
dimensions.negative_means: little or no public support; left to the market

dimensions.name: fossil_phaseout
dimensions.description: Whether fossil fuel use and production are being wound down.
dimensions.negative_means: continued or expanded fossil fuel production and use
